title: AAPD Warned Project 2025 Could Threaten Disability Supports
description_short: AAPD said Project 2025 Medicaid funding and home-care proposals could threaten supports used by people with disabilities.
description_medium: On October 29, 2024, the American Association of People with Disabilities described Project 2025 proposals to shift Medicaid to block-grant or per-capita funding and to limit home- and community-based services. AAPD warned that the proposals could constrain services used by disabled people. This is an attributed warning about proposed policy; the source does not establish later enactment or implementation.
description_long: On October 29, 2024, the American Association of People with Disabilities (AAPD) published a policy brief about Project 2025 and its potential effects on disabled people. In its Medicaid section, AAPD said the plan sought to shift Medicaid toward block-grant or per-capita funding, and proposed narrowing access to home- and community-based services (HCBS). The brief explains that many disabled people rely on Medicaid-funded HCBS to live independently. AAPD warned that restricting Medicaid funding and HCBS eligibility could limit supports for people with disabilities. The warning describes projected consequences if proposals were adopted, not completed government actions. The supplied materials do not establish that the Trump administration abolished ADA accommodations or enforcement, enacted the Medicaid cuts in the prior description, caused a specific number of coverage losses, or forced people into institutions. They also do not show which, if any, of the proposals later became policy. This entry is therefore narrowed to AAPD's attributed 2024 warning about a policy blueprint, without presenting forecasts as realized harm or attributing the blueprint's proposals to a specific administration action.

title: DHS Rescinds Protected-Areas Guidance for Immigration Enforcement
description_short: Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman rescinded 2021 guidance limiting immigration enforcement in or near protected areas.
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman issued a memorandum rescinding the 2021 guidance for immigration enforcement in or near protected areas. DHS said the change applied to ICE and CBP and directed officers to use enforcement discretion without the prior bright-line rules. This supports a policy change, not claims that Tom Homan personally ordered raids or that specific collateral harms occurred.
description_long: On January 20, 2025, Acting Department of Homeland Security Secretary Benjamine C. Huffman issued an immediate memorandum titled “Enforcement Actions in or Near Protected Areas.” The memo superseded and rescinded the October 27, 2021 DHS guidance for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection actions in or near areas previously designated for special protection. The memo says officers should continue using enforcement discretion and states that agency heads need not create “bright line rules” about where immigration laws may be enforced. DHS described the change as rescinding the Biden administration’s guidelines for enforcement in or near “sensitive” areas, including schools and churches. These records establish a change to department policy and expanded discretion at those locations. They do not establish that Border Czar Tom Homan personally ordered raids at churches or schools, how many such operations occurred, that families were separated as a result, or that advocates documented hundreds of collateral-harm cases. This entry is limited to the documented rescission and avoids turning a change in enforcement guidance into an unsupported account of specific raids or outcomes.

source_fact_map.fact: Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman issued the memo on January 20, 2025, effective immediately, rescinding the 2021 guidance.
source_fact_map.quote: This memorandum supersedes and rescinds Alejandro Mayorkas's October 27,2021 memorandum entitled, Guidelines for Enforcement Actions in or Near Protected Areas.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
January 20,2025

MEMORANDUM FOR: Caleb Vitello

Acting Director U.S.Immigration and Customs Enforcement

Pete R.Flores

Senior Official Performing the Duties of the Commissioner U.S. Customs and Border Protection

FROM: Benjamine C. Huffman Acting Secretary

SUBJECT: Enforcement Actions in or Near Protected Areas

This memorandum addresses Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) enforcement actions in or near areas that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) previously determined require special protection. It is effective immediately. This memorandum supersedes and rescinds Alejandro Mayorkas's October 27, 2021 memorandum entitled, Guidelines for Enforcement Actions in or Near Protected Areas.

source_fact_map.fact: The memo no longer required agency heads to create bright-line rules governing where immigration enforcement may occur.
source_fact_map.quote: It is not necessary, however, for the head of the agency to create bright line rules regarding where our immigration laws are permitted to be enforced.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Going forward, law enforcement officers should continue to use that discretion along with a healthy dose of common sense. It is not necessary, however, for the head of the agency to create bright line rules regarding where our immigration laws are permitted to be enforced. The Director of ICE and the Commissioner of CBP may wish to issue further guidance to assist officers in exercising appropriate enforcement discretion.

source_fact_map.fact: DHS described the memo as rescinding Biden-era ICE and CBP enforcement guidance in or near sensitive areas.
source_fact_map.quote: The first directive rescinds the Biden Administration’s guidelines for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) enforcement actions that thwart law enforcement in or near so-called “sensitive” areas.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
Release Date: January 21, 2025

WASHINGTON – Yesterday, Acting Department of Homeland Security Secretary Benjamine Huffman issued two directives. The first directive rescinds the Biden Administration’s guidelines for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) enforcement actions that thwart law enforcement in or near so-called “sensitive” areas.

source_fact_map.fact: DHS's statement specifically mentioned schools and churches as locations where enforcement could occur.
source_fact_map.quote: Criminals will no longer be able to hide in America’s schools and churches to avoid arrest.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The following statement is attributable to a DHS Spokesperson: “This action empowers the brave men and women in CBP and ICE to enforce our immigration laws and catch criminal aliens—including murders and rapists—who have illegally come into our country. Criminals will no longer be able to hide in America’s schools and churches to avoid arrest. The Trump Administration will not tie the hands of our brave law enforcement, and instead trusts them to use common sense.”

title: Trump Acknowledged Istanbul Business Conflict in 2015 Interview
description_short: Trump said a major Istanbul building gave him “a little conflict of interest” when discussing Turkey in a 2015 interview.
description_medium: In a December 1, 2015 interview on Breitbart News Daily, Donald Trump said he had “a little conflict of interest” because of a major building in Istanbul called Trump Towers. This supports a public acknowledgment of a potential business conflict while discussing Turkey. It does not establish repeated Turkish-government bookings at the Istanbul property or that the business interest shaped U.S. policy toward Turkey.
description_long: On December 1, 2015, Donald Trump spoke on Breitbart News Daily about Turkey and said he had “a little conflict of interest” because he had a major building in Istanbul called Trump Towers. TIME later quoted the remark and identified it as a 2015 interview; Politico reported on a Tuesday-morning Breitbart interview on December 1, 2015. The statement documents a public acknowledgment of a potential business conflict while discussing Turkey. It does not show that Turkish government agencies or affiliated groups booked Trump Towers Istanbul during his presidency, that those bookings generated payments to Trump, or that U.S. decisions toward Turkey were made to benefit the property. The held record further alleges that Trump repeatedly favored President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan because of this business interest. The sources accessed for this repair do not establish that causal link. This account therefore records the 2015 statement and leaves the broader booking and policy-influence allegations unresolved; it does not present them as findings of corruption or proof that the property changed government policy.
date_precision: Politico reports the Breitbart interview on December 1, 2015; TIME independently dates the quoted interview to 2015.
subcategory: Disclosed foreign business interest and potential conflict

frozen_original.title: Trump Ends FEMA National Flood Insurance Program
frozen_original.claim: The Trump administration moved in March 2025 to effectively wind down the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP).

blockers: The three targeted searches and source retrievals found no evidence that the Trump administration announced or took a March 2025 action to end or wind down NFIP; the supplied hold packet also says no credible evidence reviewed supported that assertion.

FEMA's March 25, 2025 notice documents a separate action: stopping implementation of the Federal Flood Risk Management Standard for certain FEMA-funded projects. FEMA explicitly says that standard did not apply to NFIP mapping, rates, or mandatory flood-insurance purchase requirements. That action cannot support the original NFIP wind-down claim and is not substituted as the event.

The Congressional Research Service's March 21, 2025 NFIP brief states authorization continued through September 30, 2025 and lists the March 14, 2025 continuing resolution among NFIP extensions; a contemporaneous National Association of Home Builders report also says the March legislation extended NFIP authorization through September 30. This conflicts with the entry's claim that the program was effectively ended in March.

Two supplied FEMA service URLs could not be used as direct confirmation in this run: the NFIP Direct portal returned no extractable content from Exa, and the supplied Group Flood Insurance page returned CRAWL_NOT_FOUND (404). I do not rely on the earlier hold's portal-operating assertion as an independently verified fact.

supporting_sources.excerpt: The Federal Flood Risk Management Standard had no effect on FEMA’s Flood Insurance Rate Maps as it does not apply to the National Flood Insurance Program's mapping process. In addition, the process of updating or creating a flood map is not impacted by this rescission. The FFRMS did not affect National Flood Insurance Program premium rates or inform mandatory flood insurance purchase requirements.
